goal: Add continuous integration builds for the Guix reproducible build system.
Catch release build and codesign environment breakages before release time.
reviewability: The branch passes CI and the author has requested review on the current approach.
agreement: Positive with concept support from maintainers (fanquake, sedited).
Author raised an open question regarding relying on personal substitute servers.

categories.name: build
why: P2 because it automates verification of the Guix release toolchain in CI.
Guix build and codesigning failures will be caught on PRs instead of during release cycles.

result.summary: Adds a standalone GitHub Actions workflow that executes single-host Guix reproducible builds for Linux, macOS, and Windows. It exports Guix time-machine metadata from prelude.bash for cache key generation and substitute servers, establishes caching for Guix bootstraps and dependencies, and verifies codesign environments inside containers without requiring release signing keys.
result.problem: Guix build and codesigning manifest regressions currently go unnoticed until release time because Guix is not built in regular CI workflows. Release builders and contributors face unexpected build failures during release preparation.

open_concerns: Whether CI should rely exclusively on two substitute servers hosted by the author or also query upstream substitute servers at the expense of longer job runtime.
resolved_concerns: Potential overlap with PR 35929 regarding depends caching and toolchain metadata was resolved by rebasing on 35929.

reviewability.label: Ready
reviewability.reason: The patch is clean, CI passes, and the author explicitly marked the PR ready for review.

agreement.summary: Positive concept feedback with an open question on substitute server infrastructure.
agreement.reason: fanquake and sedited have provided Concept ACKs with no objections raised. The only open point is an operational decision raised by the author regarding substitute server reliance.
evidence: willcl-ark noted the main open question is whether relying on two author-operated Guix substitute servers is acceptable to maintainers.

enables: Continuous CI validation of Guix reproducible release builds across supported platforms.

categories.name: build
categories.evidence: Touches .github/workflows/guix.yml, .github/install-guix.sh, and contrib/guix/libexec/prelude.bash to add Guix build automation.
categories.rationale: Automating Guix builds in CI provides direct protection for release integrity by catching build and codesign regressions on every PR. The Guix toolchain produces Bitcoin Core's official release binaries, and detecting breakages continuously rather than at release tagging avoids release delays.

categories.name: tests
categories.evidence: CI workflow definitions and release build automation belong to the build category rather than test framework machinery.
categories.rationale: CI configuration and scripts are explicitly handled under build; this PR does not modify test runners, fuzzers, or test suite infrastructure.

categories.name: tools
categories.evidence: The category definition explicitly notes that build and release scripts belong to build rather than tools.
categories.rationale: Changes to contrib/guix scripts are release build infrastructure covered by the build category.

result.card: Adds a standalone GitHub Actions workflow running single-host Guix builds for Linux, macOS, and Windows to catch release build and manifest breakages in CI. It solves the problem of Guix build failures going undetected until release time by providing automated verification and dependency caching. Concept ACKs have been provided by maintainers, with an open discussion on whether CI should rely entirely on author-operated Guix substitute servers. The PR is clean and ready for review.
